call.text: Figure 1 shows a two‑stage hierarchical design (S=2) and Dynamic Chunking (DC); the bottom‑right key components of a chunking layer are a routing module for dynamically drawing chunk boundaries and a downsampler that selectively retains vectors based on boundary indicators, reducing sequence length while preserving semantically significant positions [HNET:1:c012]. H‑Net (2-stage) is significantly better than H‑Net (1-stage), validating that iterated dynamic chunking can potentially learn a nested hierarchy of useful features, and leverage compute and parameters even more effectively [HNET:3.1:c049].
